slot.brief: Evaluate a composite inverse trig expression (like tan⁻¹ inside another inverse) using the right-triangle method and identity substitution.

verdicts.working: The first term is \(\tan^{-1}(2/3)\). Also, \(\sin^{-1}(\cos(\tan^{-1}(3/4)))=\sin^{-1}(4/5)=\tan^{-1}(4/3)\). Their sum has tangent \((2/3+4/3)/(1-8/9)=18\), and the sum lies in the principal range, so it equals \(\tan^{-1}(18)\).

working:
$\sin(\cos^{-1}\dfrac{5}{13})=\dfrac{12}{13},\quad \cos(\cos^{-1}\dfrac{5}{13})=\dfrac{5}{13}$, so the first term is $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2}{3}$. $\cos(\tan^{-1}\dfrac{3}{4})=\dfrac{4}{5}$, so the second term is $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{4}{3}$. $\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot\dfrac{4}{3}=\dfrac{8}{9}<1$; hence the sum is in $(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2})$. $\tan(\text{sum})=\dfrac{\dfrac{2}{3}+\dfrac{4}{3}}{1-\dfrac{8}{9}}=18$; the value is $\tan^{-1}(18)$.

Independent check: The first term is \(\tan^{-1}(2/3)\). Also, \(\sin^{-1}(\cos(\tan^{-1}(3/4)))=\sin^{-1}(4/5)=\tan^{-1}(4/3)\). Their sum has tangent \((2/3+4/3)/(1-8/9)=18\), and the sum lies in the principal range, so it equals \(\tan^{-1}(18)\).
solution:
Using the principal inverse-trigonometric ranges, the two terms are $\tan^{-1}(2/3)$ and $\tan^{-1}(4/3)$.
$$\tan\bigl(\tan^{-1}(2/3)+\tan^{-1}(4/3)\bigr)=\frac{2/3+4/3}{1-(2/3)(4/3)}=18.$$
Since their sum lies in $(0,\frac{\pi}{2})$, the expression equals $\tan^{-1}(18)$.
